verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 rocket is known as the Space Launch System (SLS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket" (R1); "SLS rocket that fired the Artemis II crew" (R2); "The Space Launch System rocket, which is being used by Artemis II" (R3); "NASA is set to launch the Space Launch System rocket, part of its Artemis program" (R4); "The entire stack known as SLS, or Space Launch System" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly identify the Artemis II rocket as the SLS.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket" (R1); "NASA's Space Launch System rocket" (R2); "NASA's Space Launch System (SLS)" (R3); "NASA is set to launch the Space Launch System rocket, part of its Artemis program" (R4); "NASA’s Space Launch System" (R6); "NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) heavy-lift rocket" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources describe SLS as NASA's rocket/program.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Boeing is responsible for building the core stage (and just most of the rocket, really)"; "Boeing builds the rockets in New Orleans."
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly states Boeing built the core stage.

verifications.claim: Northrop Grumman provided the solid rocket boosters.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Northrop Grumman is building the solid boosters on the side." (R4); "Built by Northrup Grumman in Promontory, Utah" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Both R4 and R6 explicitly credit Northrop Grumman with the solid rocket boosters.

verifications.claim: United Launch Alliance built the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion System upper stage.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the interim cryogenic propulsion stage, is built by United Launch Alliance" (R4); "The ICPS is built by United Launch Alliance (ULA)" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R4 and R6 directly confirm United Launch Alliance built the ICPS.

verifications.claim: The core stage was developed at NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The Core Stage: Built in New Orleans at the Michoud Assembly Facility"
verifications.reasoning: R6 states it was built at Michoud; 'developed' is closely supported by 'built' at the NASA facility.

verifications.claim: The core stage is the largest part of the rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the core stage (the bulk of the rocket—if you pointed at random at a part of SLS, you’d probably hit the core stage)" (R4); "the Core Stage of SLS is the largest component of the entire stack" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Both sources describe the core stage as the largest/bulk component.

verifications.claim: The core stage features four RS-25 engines.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The engines on the core stage were built for the space shuttle program. ... Shuttle RS-25 engines" (R3); "At its base, it holds four RS-25 engines" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R6 directly states four RS-25 engines on core stage; R3 supports RS-25 on core.

verifications.claim: The solid rocket boosters are 5-segment solid rocket boosters derived from the Space Shuttle program.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "they are basically the same ones used on the Space Shuttle" (R4); "these boosters are built in segments, which again are left overs from the shuttle program" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm derived from Shuttle program and segmented, but do not specify '5-segment'; broader description supports derivation.

verifications.claim: The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion System (ICPS) provides the final push to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the interim cryogenic propulsion stage fired its main engine ... raising the ... orbit"; "Orion separates from interim cryogenic propulsion stage" (R1); "The ICPS ignites after the Core Stage is jettisoned and will send Orion all the way to the Moon" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R6 directly states ICPS sends Orion to the Moon; R1 describes its burns for translunar trajectory.

verifications.claim: Aerojet Rocketdyne built the RS-25 engines for the core stage.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Aerojet Rocketdyne is building the engines" (R4); "four RS-25 engines built by Aerojet Rocketdyne" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Both directly attribute RS-25 engines to Aerojet Rocketdyne for SLS/core stage.

verifications.claim: Lockheed Martin built the crew capsule for Artemis 2.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Lockheed Martin-built Orion crew capsule" (R4); "Lockheed Martin is the prime contractor building Orion" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Lockheed Martin built Orion crew capsule for Artemis.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will carry the crew during the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the crew is spending ... orbiting the Earth while they put their Orion capsule through its paces" (R1); "Orion capsule ... carrying people" (R2); "will launch a test model of the Lockheed Martin-built Orion crew capsule" (R4); "Orion spacecraft holds the crew for Artemis missions" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources state Orion carries the Artemis II crew.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket making its first crewed launch" (R1); "NASA calls that plan Artemis. ... human spaceflight" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: First crewed SLS launch confirms it is human-rated for crewed missions.
